Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Start: 11:00 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Quantum Bridge Head of Partnerships), Nadia Singh (Channel Sales), Ethan Park (Solutions Architect), Sara Lee (BD)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Joint pipeline review: 4 active opportunities discussed (Acme, Meridian Health, Tempo Retail, Solari Fintech)
- Agreement on joint outreach cadence and lead routing; need referral/pricing sheet
- Technical follow-ups: latency/cost estimate for Acme PoC, SSO/SAML details, private deployment questions for Solari
- Next steps: pricing worksheet, enablement session, benchmarks for PoC

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): alright everyone thanks for joining on a short holiday week, we'll keep this tight. quick roll call, and we'll go into the deals.
00:12 Liam (Quantum Bridge): hey hey, got it, thanks Maya.
00:15 Tom (Redwood SE): morning all, Tom here.
00:18 Nadia (Quantum Bridge): Nadia here.
00:22 Maya: cool, objective for today is pipeline sync + figure out who owns what outreach and any blocker items for the four joint opps we talked about.
00:31 Ethan (Quantum Bridge): sounds good.
00:35 01:05 Maya: first up Acme Corp - status? we had a joint intro earlier this month, Acme's looking for a generative search assistant across product docs and support tickets. Nadia, what's the update on Acme from your side?
01:15 Nadia: Acme is in evaluation - they liked the demo. major checkboxes are security and latency. they're leaning enterprise, want SOC two evidence and SSO integration. they also asked about private deployment options for data residency.
01:30 Maya: great, we can cover SOC 2 and SSO - we'll share SOC two pack and SAML SSO flow. latency is more of a runtime question - Tom can you give a rough estimate for hosted vs dedicated?
01:42 Tom: yeah so back of envelope: for their 2k token average sessions, hosted API with our mid-tier model is hitting ~110-130ms per token p50 on our EU region - oh sorry i said p50 per token, i mean p50 latency per response segment, there's some transcription noise - but for throughput and cost: dedicated fixed pool reduces unit cost by ~30% depending on batch config. i'll run a specific estimate for Acme's volume and share a spreadsheet.
02:10 Ethan: are you guys using KV cash or cache? i saw notes saying KV cash in the deck, just want to confirm caching behavior for prefix reuse.
02:18 Tom: yes that's KV cache - sorry the transcript in the deck had a typo. we do prefix/KV caching which should drastically reduce tokens for repeated queries. will include that in the cost calc.
02:30 Maya: good, next Meridian Health - bigger compliance ask, they require ISO 27001 and on-prem options for a scope of certain PHI workloads. Liam are you owning Meridian outreach?
02:43 Liam: yes we'll take Meridian. quick flag: Meridian is very health-regulated, so private deployment or V P C peering is almost mandatory. Redwood private deployment and KMS integration was one of the selling points we used.
03:00 Priya (Redwood CSM): we should prep a short checklist for Meridian: SOC2, ISO cert snips, KMS/HSM support, log retention and audit hooks. i can draft.
03:12 Nadia: also include runbook for incident response and data deletion timelines.
03:18 Maya: noted. Solari Fintech - big spend possibility but very latency sensitive and wants predictable SLAs. they asked about dedicated pools + guaranteed SLOs and cold-start behavior for large models. Tom, thoughts?
03:34 Tom: dedicated is the route for Solari. we can offer reserved capacity with autoscaling policies and burst buffers. cold start depends on the model variant; for 70B-like variants bootstrapping KV cache can take a few seconds for first loads but after warmup p95 is much better. also can pin a warm instance for critical routes.
03:55 Ethan: on the compliance for Solari, do you support tenant-level audit logs and KMS key separation?
04:02 Maya: yes, private + dedicated gives those controls; we'll provide documentation.
04:08 Sara (Quantum Bridge): for Solari we want to co-sell a bundled offering - how do you structure referral credits vs reseller discounts?
04:16 Maya: good question - we typically do a referral kickback model for partner-sourced net-new ARR on first 12 months plus a discounted seat rate for joint engagements. i'll send the joint pricing worksheet. for larger enterprise commits we can do deeper discounts under reserved capacity contracts.
04:36 Liam: can we align on lead routing? we want dedicated routing for partner-sourced leads, and a shared deal registration sheet so both teams get credit.
04:46 Maya: absolutely. we'll create a shared Google sheet + CRM tagging pattern and Maya will update the deal registration process.
04:52 05:10 Tom: small technical ask - Acme asked for a performance bench run on their sample data for reranking and embeddings. we can run a benchmark but need their sample dataset and some expected QPS.
05:22 Nadia: i'll get the sample over. expect it'll be a low to medium qps test to start, maybe 10-20 reqs per second.
05:30 Priya: i'll map out pilot success criteria - accuracy on rerank vs baseline, 95th percentile latency target, and cost per 1k queries.
05:40 Maya: awesome. other competitive concerns? any objections we should coordinate on?
05:45 Sara: Acme mentioned they also are talking to Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted models; they asked about vendor lock and portability.
05:54 Maya: we should emphasize model portability and ability to run private or dedicated; highlight our model catalog and model variants for cost-performance tradeoffs. Tom can add technical notes on quantization and kernel selection.
06:10 Tom: yes, we'll prepare a short slide on migration/portability and quant profiles.
06:20 Maya: logistics for enablement - Nadia, you asked for a sales enablement session for your channel reps?
06:25 Nadia: yes, ideally Jan 7th, 90 minutes, covering product differentiators, pricing model, and common objection handling for security and latency.
06:34 Maya: we'll do that - Priya and I will lead, Tom will join for the tech deep-dive. I'll send a calendar invite after the pricing sheet is out.
06:45 07:00 Liam: question on reporting and console - do you expose per-token cost breakdown per route so our reps can quote accurately?
07:08 Maya: yes Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model; we can create a shared dashboard view for Quantum Bridge.
07:16 Sara: perfect.
07:22 Maya: wrap up - recap of action items: Maya to share pricing worksheet and referral model by 12/27; Tom to deliver Acme latency/cost spreadsheet by 12/30 and run bench after we get sample; Priya to draft pilot success criteria by 1/4; Nadia to send target list and Acme sample by 12/29; schedule enablement Jan 7th. any final Qs?
07:44 Ethan: none from me.
07:46 Liam: nope, thanks all.
07:48 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and post the sheet. Happy holidays.
